units.note: English omits πρὸς τὸν στρατηγόν (they pressed the praetor); omission outside the error classes, not filed.

findings.quote: I think you would find no one among us better suited to stand beside you and help you.
findings.problem: μηδένα συναγωνιστὴν καὶ συνεργὸν ἄλλον εὑρεῖν ἂν ἡμῶν ἐπιτηδειότερον: ἡμῶν is a genitive of comparison ('no one ... more suitable than me'). Polybius is offering himself; 'among us' turns his offer into a general remark.
findings.proposed_fix: I think you would find no one better suited than me to stand beside you and help you.

findings.quote: This ambition first came into prominence at the time we are speaking of,
findings.problem: συνέβη δὲ τὴν παροῦσαν αἵρεσιν οἷον ἐκλάμψαι: 'the present tendency' is the extravagance just described (Macedonian wealth and unrivalled power are given as its causes), not Scipio's ambition. Also, πρῶτον μὲν introduces the first reason; it does not mean the tendency 'first' appeared then.
findings.proposed_fix: This tendency blazed out, as it were, at the time we are speaking of,

units.note: ἀναλαβεῖν rendered 'recover' (better 'win'); minor and not filed.

findings.quote: Scipio gave to his mother, who had long since been separated from Lucius
findings.problem: The Greek has a lacuna: ἐδωρήσατο τῇ μητρί, *** ᾗ συνέβαινε κεχωρίσθαι. The English reads straight through without marking the gap (editors usually supply her name, Papiria).
findings.proposed_fix: Scipio gave to his mother [...], who had long since been separated from Lucius

findings.quote: But when he insisted that Scipio had given exactly those instructions, they believed him and went on to the young man
findings.problem: διαπιστήσαντες προῆγον ἐπὶ τὸν νεανίσκον: διαπιστήσαντες means 'disbelieving'. They did not believe the banker, and that is why they went to Scipio. The English reverses this.
findings.proposed_fix: But when he insisted that Scipio had given exactly those instructions, they did not believe him and went on to the young man

findings.quote: After this, he was obliged to pay the remaining half of the dowries owed to the daughters of Scipio the Great, who were the sisters of his adoptive father.
findings.problem: The Greek has a lacuna: ἀδελφαῖς δὲ τοῦ κατὰ θέσιν πατρός, *** λαβόντος, αὐτὸν ἔδει. A genitive participle clause (someone 'having received/inherited') is lost. The English smooths over it.
findings.proposed_fix: After this, he was obliged to pay the remaining half of the dowries owed to the daughters of Scipio the Great, who were the sisters of his adoptive father [...].

units.note: προδοθέντων πρώτων τῶν ἐπίπλων εἰς δέκα μῆνας is rendered 'the furniture had first been sold'. It means that the movables were first handed over (paid) within ten months, not sold. This is a lexical error outside the error classes, so it is not filed; the orchestrator may want to review it.
